unlisted_practices: Establish a new integrative medical specialty, ICT medicine, with ICT doctors who bridge ICT professionals and clinical users.
Create independent ICT medicine institutes within health care organizations to counterbalance the power of commercial ICT companies and reduce dependency on vendors.
Have ICT doctors coordinate dispersed digital activities across hospital departments to prevent uncontrolled growth and duplication of e-health projects and promote standardization.
Continuously study the patterns of interaction between doctors, patients, and adaptive AI algorithms.
Have ICT doctors supervise medical data collection and sharing and guide multidisciplinary verification of AI inputs and outputs.
Audit generalist medical AI models for inaccuracies, misstatements, and social biases.
Research the reproducibility of clinical diagnostic and prognostic AI tools and facilitate open and transparent AI systems in health care.
Adjust AI algorithms to local patient populations and health care facilities.
Develop open-source generative AI models in cooperation with public or nonprofit ICT specialists without commercial input.
Promote digital inclusion by overcoming structural barriers relating to age, race, socioeconomic status, and language skills.

screen.reason: This is a personal viewpoint paper proposing the creation of a new medical specialty ('ICT medicine') to guide, validate, and safeguard AI and digital technology implementation in healthcare.
